meta.name: Bespoke Perfume Question Graph
meta.opening_promise: Fifteen questions. You won’t need to name a single note.
meta.act_transition_copy: Good. I know how you want to be worn. Now tell me where you've been.
meta.expert_deepdive_note: Fluency is detected first, before Act I. Confirmed perfumers (fluency_score >= 5 by GATE-narrative) skip the anchor/accent/texture memory tree entirely (GATE-narrative -> I-veto) and, after the veto/anosmia inserts, answer a style question (I-expert-style) branching into one of eleven technical deep-dive paths (oud, mukhallat, amber, chypre, fougere, gourmand, forest, dark, fresh, all-day, projection, romance) before a 3-candidate preview. Lover/enthusiast customers take the original single B1->B2->B3 memory-tree path and never see the style branch.
meta.echo_note: Options may carry `echo`: one line handed back to the customer after they choose it. Rendered by fluency tier — a perfumer hears note_to_perfumer verbatim, an enthusiast hears its first sentence, a lover hears `echo`. Deliberately not on every option: an acknowledgement after all fifteen answers is wallpaper by the fourth.

B3-rain-deep.text: Then tell me which rain. They are not the same rain.

options.label: The first one. Dust rising before the drops land
options.note_to_perfumer: Attar Mitti (the genuine Kannauj clay attar) for the ground, Geosmin at trace for the exact moment rain lands, Floralozone for the air just before. The dust must arrive before the water.

options.label: The long monsoon. Four days without stopping
Forest rain — cold, green, and older than you
options.note_to_perfumer: Pine EO, cypriol, vetiver, peatmoss. Cold not fresh.

options.label: The drench. Soaked to the skin, laughing
options.note_to_perfumer: Petrichor's ozone and crushed grass at the top, but instead of drying into earth and wood, this settles into a warm, clean skin-musk — ambroxan and exaltolide instead of geosmin and cedarwood at the base. Rain that stays close, not rain that becomes ground.

options.label: Rain you watched from inside, through glass
options.note_to_perfumer: The rain is remembered, not felt. Pull geosmin to trace, push musk.

options.label: The first smell of it — mitti, with the flowers just starting to open
options.note_to_perfumer: Attar Mitti and geosmin at trace for the exact moment dust meets water, but this time jasmine sambac opens right alongside it — the rain doesn't arrive alone, the flowers open the second it does.

options.label: Rain still falling, cool and steady — flowers heavy with it
options.note_to_perfumer: Rose Wardia and geraniol heavy with rainwater, vetiver's wet root underneath — the middle of the rain, not the start or the end, when everything is thoroughly, steadily wet.

options.label: After it's passed — cool wind, and the flowers finally open
options.note_to_perfumer: The rain has passed — floralozone and dihydromyrcenol for the washed, cool wind, jasmine finally opening now that the storm's gone, geosmin fading to almost nothing. The clearing, not the storm.

B2-wedding.text: A wedding is fifty smells at once. Which one reached you?

options.label: Mehndi night. Green paste, oil, staying up too late
Haldi. Turmeric on skin, marigold underfoot
The aunties' perfume. Sharp, and unforgettable
The food tent. Biryani smoke over everything
Bidaai. The car door closing
options.note_to_perfumer: Flowers going over, exhaust, someone's perfume leaving the room. Overblown rose + jasmine, a metallic aldehyde edge, musk that outlasts them both.

options.label: Kewra sherbet, passed around in small steel glasses
options.note_to_perfumer: Attar Kewra — the real pandanus-flower attar, sweet and slightly medicinal-green — with rose and a whisper of cardamom, exactly how the sherbet tastes at a wedding. Benzoin rounds the sweetness so it isn't just syrup.

B3-mehendi-deep.text: Which part of the mehendi night?

options.label: Flowers and fountains in the courtyard, food just starting to arrive

options.label: A royal wedding — everything at once: flowers, spice, dessert, water in the air
options.note_to_perfumer: The whole wedding in one bottle — rose, jasmine, and kewra for the flowers, cardamom and safraleine for the spice, benzoin and vanillin for the dessert table, cashmeran and ethylene brassylate underneath so it still reads as a perfume and not just a room. options.label: Just the paste itself — green, herbal, drying on warm skin
options.note_to_perfumer: Just the paste — clary sage and cis-3-hexenyl acetate for the crushed-leaf green, patchouli and vetiver underneath as it dries and warms on skin.

B3-attars-deep.text: Which kind of room was it?

options.label: Ivory and jasmine — soft, clean, nothing dark
options.note_to_perfumer: Soft, creamy, and luminous — ebanol and bacdanol's clean sandalwood-musk instead of a dark, resinous oud. Jasmine sambac and hedione keep it wearable in daylight.

options.label: Amber gone gold with age, resin thick in the air

options.label: Rose pressed into the walls, years of it
options.note_to_perfumer: A true rose mukhallat — Rose Wardia at the center, real oud and agarwood only a shadow underneath so the rose is never in doubt.

options.label: Incense still hanging in the air
options.note_to_perfumer: Real frankincense and myrrh over oud and agarwood — the incense-room mukhallat, dry and resinous rather than sweet.

options.label: Spice in every corner of the room
options.note_to_perfumer: Cardamom and black pepper over oud and agarwood, safraleine's saffron-leather threading through — the spice-market mukhallat.

options.label: Mango, ripe and creamy

options.label: Peach, soft and velvety

options.label: Green apple, fresh and sharp

I-veto.text: Before I build this — is there anything I should stay away from?

options.echo: Nothing off-limits. Then we can use the difficult things.

I-reapply.text: When you wear something you love, do you reapply during the day?
I-reapply.text_gift: When they wear something they love, do they reapply during the day, if you've noticed?

options.label: Yes, always. Usually mid-afternoon

constraint.note: wears it for themselves; reapplying all day means the formula can afford to be top-heavy and bright rather than engineered for unattended longevity — nudges toward the same materials I-expert-allday-detail's ten accords are built from

options.label: No. Once in the morning is enough
I don't own anything I love yet

constraint.note: highest-value and highest-risk customer; ship the gentler of the two candidates as the bottle

I-anosmia.text: Is there a perfume everyone raves about that you simply can't smell?
I-anosmia.text_gift: Is there a perfume everyone raves about that they simply can't smell?

options.label: Yes — and I've always wondered why
No, or not that I know of

I-expert-style.text: Is there a particular style pulling at you right now?

options.label: Ambers — resinous, warm, honeyed
Mukhallats — the full Arabic attar chord
Oud — I want it to be the point
Spices — I want to feel the market, not just smell it
Something fresh, or citrus — clean air, not heavy resin
Gourmand — sweet, but I want it to still read as a perfume
Chypre — bergamot, moss, and a mossy floor under the florals
Fougère — lavender and hay, the classic barbershop structure
Romance — love letters, rose pressed in a book
Dark and complex — for people who live in this hobby
Mountain and forest — a cabin in the woods
Long-lasting — I want this on my skin at midnight
High projection — I want the room to know
Loud, but I reapply through the day anyway

I-expert-mukhallat-detail.text: Fruit worked into the attar chord, or the classic version untouched?

options.label: Fruit — something sweet worked into the resin and rose
No, the classic attar chord is exactly what I want
Dark berries steeped into the rose-oud chord
options.note_to_perfumer: Dark berries steeped into a genuine rose-oud attar — blackcurrant and damascone's jammy top over Rose Wardia, oud and agarwood only a shadow underneath, ethylene brassylate and exaltolide holding the whole chord together.

options.label: Mango, ripe and creamy, folded into the attar
options.note_to_perfumer: Creamy tropical mango folded into the rose-oud-musk chord rather than a plain oud base — gamma-undecalactone and fructone for the fruit, the full attar structure still doing the work underneath.

options.label: Peach, soft and velvety, against the rose-musk base
options.note_to_perfumer: Soft, velvety peach against a genuine rose-musk-oud attar — the fuzzy-skin lactone facet sitting over Rose Wardia, not a bare oud drydown.

options.label: Green apple, sharp against the deep animalic base
options.note_to_perfumer: Fresh green apple cut sharp against a real rose-oud-musk chord — cis-3-hexenyl acetate for the bitten skin, the full attar depth still underneath rather than a quiet single-note oud.

options.label: Rose, with berries steeped underneath — the classic attar move
options.note_to_perfumer: Rose Wardia at real strength with blackcurrant steeped underneath — the fruited-rose attar move done honestly, oud and agarwood only a shadow, exactly as a mukhallat should carry them.

options.label: Bright citrus, unusual against the rose-oud base but real
options.note_to_perfumer: Bright bergamot and orange laid over the full rose-oud-musk chord — an unusual citrus-attar combination, but built honestly rather than as a plain citrus-oud.

I-expert-romance-detail.text: Which love story is it, exactly?

options.label: A love letter, the rose ink still wet
options.note_to_perfumer: Rose Wardia and geraniol at the center, hedione for the ink's own faint sweetness, exaltolide holding it close to skin rather than let it announce itself.

options.label: Rose, crushed and pressed between the pages of a book
options.note_to_perfumer: Rose Wardia flattened against cedarwood and a whisper of vetiver — the exact smell of a real flower dried inside a closed book for years, paper and petal as one note.

options.label: A wax seal, still warm, closing the envelope
options.note_to_perfumer: Benzoin and labdanum for the warm melted-wax resin, rose just behind it — the moment of sealing something, not the letter itself.

options.label: Ink and parchment — nothing living in the room but the letter
options.note_to_perfumer: Cedarwood and vetiver for dry paper and old ink, no flower at all — the room the letter was written in, not the rose it describes.

options.label: A faded photograph, the powder of an old dressing table
options.note_to_perfumer: Methyl ionone's violet-iris powder standing in for a photograph's own fade, a little benzyl acetate for the ghost of a rose, exaltolide for warm old skin.

options.label: A poem, handwritten, never sent
options.note_to_perfumer: Rose Wardia against a quiet vanilla-benzoin warmth — tender rather than declared, the poem that stayed in the drawer.

options.label: A candle left burning for someone who isn't coming back
options.note_to_perfumer: Benzoin and labdanum for melted wax and grief's own warmth, rose held underneath rather than forward — mourning, not romance exactly, but the same rose.

options.label: Violets pressed flat, years ago, still faintly there
options.note_to_perfumer: Methyl ionone gamma at real strength for true violet-iris powder, rose only a trace behind it, linalool keeping it from turning heavy.

options.label: The library where it happened — old paper, and her perfume
options.note_to_perfumer: Cedarwood and a trace of patchouli for the library itself, Rose Wardia and hedione carrying the memory of a person through the room.

options.label: First love — bright, a little nervous, rose over clean skin
options.note_to_perfumer: Rose Wardia lifted by bergamot rather than weighed down by resin, clean galaxolide-exaltolide skin underneath — young, not yet complicated.

I-expert-dark-detail.text: How dark, exactly — and in which direction?

options.label: A dark floral, animalic underneath — not for daylight
options.note_to_perfumer: Jasmine Sambac against civet at real (if trace) strength — the indolic, slightly rotten edge real jasmine already carries, pushed further rather than smoothed away.

options.label: Smoke and cold ash, the fire long out
options.note_to_perfumer: Cypriol and guaiacol for real smoke, patchouli and cedarwood for what's left in the grate afterward. No sweetness anywhere.

options.label: Skin and leather, worn in, nothing clean about it
options.note_to_perfumer: Safraleine and civet for the leather itself, norlimbanol for a dry synthetic-timber scratch underneath. Built to feel used, not new.

options.label: Patchouli taken all the way, oud underneath
options.note_to_perfumer: Patchouli at full strength rather than a supporting role, oud and agarwood as the floor underneath it — the 70s-patchouli move updated with a real oud base.

options.label: A cathedral after mass, incense still hanging in the stone
options.note_to_perfumer: Frankincense and myrrh at real strength, cypriol for the stone itself — cool, elevated smoke rather than a warm gourmand incense.

options.label: Musk the way it used to mean something — animal, not laundry
options.note_to_perfumer: Civet at real (trace) strength against exaltolide and ethylene brassylate's warmth — the pre-Galaxolide idea of musk, skin rather than clean cotton.

options.label: Amber taken to its darkest, most animalic edge
options.note_to_perfumer: Labdanum and oud together rather than labdanum alone, civet at absolute trace pushing the classic amber triangle as dark as this palette allows.

options.label: Oud with nothing softened — bitter, dry, medicinal
options.note_to_perfumer: Oud Oliffac and Agarwood Artessence at real strength with cypriol's ink and norlimbanol's dry scratch — no rose, no sweetness, nothing to make it easier.

options.label: Tobacco and old leather, a study lined with both
options.note_to_perfumer: No true tobacco absolute in this palette, so the hay-and-honey facet is reconstructed from coumarin against patchouli and labdanum's leather — an honest approximation, not a copy.

options.label: One idea, worked until it needs nothing else
options.note_to_perfumer: The minimalist 'molecule' niche move — Iso E Super pushed to a real, almost improper dose with only ambroxan and a trace of norlimbanol for company. For someone who wants the idea, not a composition.

I-expert-forest-detail.text: Which part of the woods, exactly?

options.label: A cabin, the fire lit, cedar walls holding the smoke in
options.note_to_perfumer: Cedarwood at real strength with guaiacol's smoke worked in at a bare trace, patchouli and benzoin for the room's own warmth. The whole scene, not just the fire.

options.label: Pine, straight and cold, nothing else in the air
options.note_to_perfumer: Pine EO against cedarwood and vetiver rather than a sweetened 'Christmas tree' pine — a real, slightly bitter conifer forest.

options.label: Campfire smoke, caught in a sweater the next morning
options.note_to_perfumer: Guaiacol at real strength for genuine woodsmoke, cypriol and patchouli underneath, coumarin's hay-sweetness for the marshmallow-adjacent memory.

options.label: Mountain air, thin and cold, before the treeline
options.note_to_perfumer: Floralozone and dihydromyrcenol for the thin, ozone-cold high-altitude air, pine only a low hum underneath.

options.label: The forest floor — wet leaves, root, and soil
options.note_to_perfumer: Patchouli and vetiver for the damp ground, geosmin at a bare trace for the exact smell of leaf litter after rain, peatmoss for the moss underneath it all.

options.label: Snow settling on pine, cold and clean and green
options.note_to_perfumer: Pine EO under floralozone and dihydromyrcenol's cold sparkle, galaxolide for the hush snowfall brings rather than silence.

options.label: The cabin's own walls — cedar, and years of woodsmoke
options.note_to_perfumer: Cedarwood and Vertofix at real strength with guaiacol at the barest trace — the structure itself, long after anyone last lit a fire in it.

options.label: An alpine meadow — green and floral and short-lived
options.note_to_perfumer: Clary sage and petitgrain for the meadow's own bitter-green, geraniol and hedione for the wildflowers that only last a few weeks a year up there.

options.label: Woodsmoke and whiskey — the cabin's other fireplace
options.note_to_perfumer: Guaiacol's smoke against coumarin and benzoin's warmth — the whiskey poured once everyone's come in from the cold.

options.label: Something colder and stranger — the sky itself, not the ground
options.note_to_perfumer: Ambroxan and floralozone for something closer to atmosphere than forest — abstract, mineral, the one entry in this set that looks up instead of down.

I-expert-longlasting-detail.text: Which one should still be there tomorrow morning?

options.label: Musk built to still be there tomorrow morning
options.note_to_perfumer: Exaltolide, habanolide, and ethylene brassylate all at real strength together — three different macrocyclic musks stacked rather than one doing all the work.

options.label: Amber with a fixative base heavy enough to last the whole day
options.note_to_perfumer: Labdanum and benzoin's usual amber warmth, but with exaltolide and ethylene brassylate doing the holding instead of relying on the resins alone.

options.label: Oud with almost nothing volatile left in the formula
options.note_to_perfumer: Oud Oliffac and Agarwood Artessence anchored by exaltolide and ethylene brassylate rather than any top note at all — built to survive, not to open beautifully.

options.label: Skin-musk that survives a shower and comes back that evening
options.note_to_perfumer: Bacdanol's creamy sandalwood-musk against exaltolide and ambroxan — the specific 'ghost scent' effect of a fixative this heavy reactivating on warm skin.

options.label: Citrus, but engineered to outlast every citrus that came before it
options.note_to_perfumer: Bergamot and orange kept deliberately light on top, exaltolide and ethylene brassylate doing all the real work underneath — citrus's oldest problem solved by brute-force fixative rather than a clever trick.

options.label: A soft, velvet base heavy enough to anchor anything sprayed over it
options.note_to_perfumer: Cashmeran at real strength against Iso E Super and ambroxan — soft, spiced, and built specifically to hold other things down rather than stand alone.

options.label: Rose that doesn't fade by lunchtime
options.note_to_perfumer: Rose Wardia at real strength held up by exaltolide and ethylene brassylate in equal measure — the flower itself doesn't get to fade first.

options.label: Vanilla with a fixative base instead of a top-note burst
options.note_to_perfumer: Vanillin and benzoin's usual sweetness, but built on ethylene brassylate and exaltolide rather than a shallow gourmand base that burns off in an hour.

options.label: A dry wood built entirely around holding power
options.note_to_perfumer: Vertofix and vetiver's dry depth locked in with ethylene brassylate and exaltolide — dryness that survives rather than a wood that opens dry and fades soft.

options.label: The heaviest fixative combination this palette allows
options.note_to_perfumer: Norlimbanol, ambroxan, exaltolide, and ethylene brassylate together at real strength — the ceiling of what this palette's fixatives can do, all at once.

I-expert-projection-detail.text: Which one should announce itself first?

options.label: Built to fill the room before you've finished walking into it
options.note_to_perfumer: Iso E Super pushed to a genuinely high dose, ambroxan and sylvamber both layered on top for maximum diffusion rather than one projection material carrying the whole formula.

options.label: Oud pushed outward instead of held close
options.note_to_perfumer: Oud Oliffac and Agarwood Artessence carried on a heavy Iso E Super and ambroxan base — oud reworked to project rather than sit close to skin the way it usually does.

options.label: Every projection material this palette has, working together
options.note_to_perfumer: Sylvamber, ambroxan, and habanolide stacked together — the single loudest combination in the library.

options.label: Clean, loud, unmistakable the second you walk in
options.note_to_perfumer: Habanolide and galaxolide both at real strength, hedione for radiance — clean rather than dark, but genuinely loud.

options.label: Amber that projects instead of sitting close to skin
options.note_to_perfumer: Labdanum and benzoin's warmth carried outward on a real Iso E Super and ambroxan dose — the amber accord rebuilt for throw, not intimacy.

options.label: Spice built to trail behind you down the hallway
options.note_to_perfumer: Cardamom and black pepper lifted by a heavy Iso E Super and ambroxan base so the spice itself carries into the next room.

options.label: A floral loud enough to be a broadcast, not a whisper
options.note_to_perfumer: Rose Wardia and jasmine sambac carried on a genuinely high hedione and Iso E Super dose — the amplifier effect pushed as far as it goes.

options.label: Dry wood turned into a beacon instead of a background
options.note_to_perfumer: Cedarwood and Vertofix under a heavy sylvamber and Iso E Super load — dry wood built to be noticed across a room, not just close up.

options.label: Sweetness with real throw, not just a close warm skin-scent
options.note_to_perfumer: Vanillin and benzoin lifted by Iso E Super and ambroxan rather than left to sit quiet and close — sweetness that actually travels.

options.label: An entrance, built the way the first line of a symphony is
options.note_to_perfumer: Rose Wardia and cedarwood together, carried outward on the heaviest Iso E Super and ambroxan dose in the set — the whole library's idea of a proper entrance.

I-expert-allday-detail.text: What should the burst be, each time you top it up?

options.label: A bright burst, built to be sprayed again by noon
options.note_to_perfumer: Bergamot and dihydromyrcenol with a real aldehyde C10 sparkle — meant to be vivid for two hours and reapplied rather than stretched thin to survive six.

options.label: A floral that's just as good the third time as the first
options.note_to_perfumer: Rose Wardia carried mostly on hedione and floralozone rather than a heavy fixative base — a floral that blooms freshly on each reapplication instead of building up.

options.label: Rose that wants to be reapplied, not stretched to survive alone
options.note_to_perfumer: Rose Wardia and geraniol at real, bright strength with almost no heavy base underneath — deliberately built to fade rather than linger, so the ritual of reapplying is the point.

options.label: A spice burst that tops up clean instead of muddying
options.note_to_perfumer: Cardamom and pink pepper over bergamot — a spice top note light enough that a second or third spray never turns muddy the way heavier spice bases can.

options.label: Citrus that asks for an encore rather than fighting to last
options.note_to_perfumer: Bergamot, orange, and petitgrain at full citrus-cologne strength, no attempt made to anchor it — the opposite design choice from The Marathon in the long-lasting set, on purpose.

options.label: A green burst, cut and bright, made to be topped up
options.note_to_perfumer: Cis-3-hexenyl acetate and petitgrain for the cut-green snap, floralozone for air — a green that reads as freshly cut each time, not a single long green note fading.

options.label: A heady floral that's honestly better sprayed twice
options.note_to_perfumer: Jasmine Sambac and Rose Wardia at real strength on a light hedione-galaxolide base — indolic and heady in the first twenty minutes, which is exactly why it's built to be refreshed rather than left to fade slowly.

options.label: A sweet top-note burst, not a slow warm drydown
options.note_to_perfumer: Ethyl maltol and orange for an immediate sugar-citrus burst, no benzoin or heavy resin holding it down — sweetness as a spray-and-repeat event, not an all-day base.

options.label: A cool splash, meant to be reapplied like sunscreen
options.note_to_perfumer: Dihydromyrcenol, floralozone, and aldehyde C12 MNA at real cologne strength — the classic 'splash' format this whole family belongs to, built to be topped up all day exactly like the sunscreen it's compared to.

options.label: Everything about this set in one bottle, for the committed reapplier
options.note_to_perfumer: Rose Wardia and bergamot together on a hedione-dihydromyrcenol base — floral, citrus, and aldehydic in even balance, so whichever facet the wearer notices fading, reapplying brings all three back at once.

I-expert-fresh-detail.text: What kind of fresh — and should it actually last?

options.label: Clean and marine — glassy, like sea-glass, nothing heavy
options.note_to_perfumer: Dihydromyrcenol and floralozone for the sea-glass sparkle, hedione for the dew, cedarwood and iso E super to keep it from vanishing in twenty minutes. No true marine aldehyde in the palette, so this is built from freshness materials layered rather than one 'ocean' note.

options.label: Cucumber and melon, splashy and green
options.note_to_perfumer: Cucumber's green snap from cis-3-hexenyl acetate, gamma-undecalactone for a melon-soft roundness — there's no dedicated melon or cucumber material in the palette, so both are reconstructed from adjacent green/fruity facets.

options.label: Fresh-pressed cotton, straight off the line
options.note_to_perfumer: Fresh-pressed cotton — the classic aldehyde-linalool 'clean laundry' accord, galaxolide for the fabric-softener musk everyone recognizes without naming.

options.label: Bright citrus over open water
options.note_to_perfumer: Bergamot and orange over dihydromyrcenol's sparkle — the citrus-cologne structure updated with hedione's transparency instead of a heavier classical base.

options.label: The same, but I want it to actually last past noon
options.note_to_perfumer: The same marine freshness as Ocean Glass, but anchored — ambroxan, exaltolide, and ethylene brassylate at real strength turn the top notes into an all-day skin-musk instead of a two-hour spray-and-fade.

options.label: Citrus that doesn't disappear in twenty minutes
options.note_to_perfumer: Citrus cologne's oldest problem — it disappears — solved with exaltolide and ethylene brassylate underneath at real dose, so the bergamot keeps reappearing off warm skin for hours instead of fading after the first one.

options.label: Cool water that dries down into a real, long musk
options.note_to_perfumer: Barely 'fresh' at all by the fourth hour — deliberately. Starts as cool water, dries down into a clean, long-wearing musk that's most of the point.

options.label: My skin, but cooler — and it stays
options.note_to_perfumer: 'Your skin, but cooler' — hedione's dewy transparency over a genuinely long-wearing musk base. The freshest thing that could plausibly still be there at midnight.

options.label: Toasted nuts and caramel — praline, not candy
options.note_to_perfumer: Toasted hazelnut-praline built from lactone and coumarin rather than a literal nut note, vanilla and benzoin for warmth, cashmeran and iso E super so it reads as a perfume on skin, not a dessert in a bowl.

options.label: Salted caramel — sweetness with a mineral edge
options.note_to_perfumer: Real caramel (ethyl maltol at a careful trace, not a flood) against ambroxan's dry, mineral-salt facet — the salt keeps it from ever turning into pure sugar.

options.label: Vanilla and tonka, done properly, at real strength
options.note_to_perfumer: The modern tonka-vanilla done at full strength — real vanillin and coumarin, not a compromise dose, held up by iso E super and cashmeran so it stays elegant instead of collapsing into sweetness.

options.label: Rose and honeyed pastry — floral first, dessert second
options.note_to_perfumer: Rose water and honeyed phyllo — Rose Wardia leads, gamma-nonalactone and benzyl acetate for the honey-almond syrup, cardamom threaded through. Dessert-adjacent, but rose stays the point.

options.label: Something boozy — whiskey, oak, nothing that reads as candy
options.note_to_perfumer: A boozy, grown-up gourmand — guaiacol at real trace for the charred-oak-barrel note, patchouli for the cask's depth, coumarin and benzoin for the whiskey's own sweetness. Nothing here reads as candy.

options.label: Iced coffee and vanilla — cool, not warm
options.note_to_perfumer: Cold-brew coffee and vanilla, cooled down instead of warmed up — dihydromyrcenol for the ice, coffee CO2 kept light rather than roasty. A summer gourmand, not a winter one.

I-expert-oud-detail.text: What do you want sitting with the oud?

options.label: Fruit — something sweet cutting through the dark
Vanilla — soft and sweet, not sharp
options.note_to_perfumer: Real vanilla and benzoin wrapped around oud and agarwood — soft and sweet, never sharp, with ethyl maltol at the barest trace so it stays perfume and not dessert.

options.label: Amber — resin and warmth around it
options.note_to_perfumer: Labdanum and frankincense wrapped tight around a double-oud core (Agarwood Artessence + Oud Oliffac) — ambroxan for lift, less sweet than a full mukhallat amber, more resin than musk.

options.label: Nothing — just make it darker. Animalic, heavy, real
options.note_to_perfumer: As dark as the palette goes — civet at absolute trace for real animal warmth, norlimbanol and cypriol for a dry, smoke-adjacent leather, double oud underneath. Not for daylight.

options.label: Spice — cardamom and pepper worked into it
options.note_to_perfumer: Cardamom and black pepper as an accent, not the main event — oud and agarwood stay the center, safraleine bridging the two.

options.label: Something fresh — I don't want it to feel heavy at all
options.note_to_perfumer: Oud kept deliberately light — bergamot, petitgrain, and dihydromyrcenol do most of the talking, agarwood only a low hum underneath. For the customer who wants oud's idea, not its weight.

options.label: Something sparkling — almost fizzy, like it's carbonated
options.note_to_perfumer: The 'sparkling' modern-niche trend, built honestly: aldehyde C10 and C12 for the metallic fizz, dihydromyrcenol and bergamot for the citrus pop, blackcurrant for a cola-adjacent soda note — all of it sitting on top of a dark oud base it never actually dissolves into.

I-expert-structure.text: Where should the weight of this actually sit?

options.label: Base-heavy. Let it start quiet and grow for hours
Even across all three phases
Heart-forward — the middle is the whole point
Top-present. I like knowing what I've put on

I-expert-base.text: The base — what should still be there after eight hours?

options.label: Amber — and I'll tell you exactly which kind
Clean skin-musk, nothing else competing
Dry wood, almost no sweetness
Warm and gourmand — vanilla, tonka, benzoin
Animalic and heavy — oud, civet, real weight
Earthy — moss, patchouli, root

I-expert-amber-detail.text: Which amber, exactly? They are not the same material.

options.label: Dry, mineral, almost salty
options.note_to_perfumer: Dry, mineral, almost salty — ambroxan and vetiver instead of the usual sweet resins. The amber family's driest possible reading.

options.label: Dark, leathery, honeyed
options.note_to_perfumer: Dark, leathery, honeyed — labdanum and safraleine for the leather, civet at absolute trace for real warmth, benzoin so it never turns dry. The amber a saddle would smell like.

options.label: Sweet, powdery, vanillic
options.note_to_perfumer: Sweet, powdery, unapologetically vanillic — vanillin and benzoin at real strength, coumarin for the powder, labdanum keeping it from turning into dessert.

options.label: Woody and austere — barely sweet at all
Dense and animalic — amber with an oud shadow
Honeyed and thick, almost edible without tipping into dessert
options.note_to_perfumer: Labdanum and benzoin pushed to their thickest, most honeyed edge — ethyl maltol at a bare trace for sweetness, civet at homeopathic trace for warmth, without ever tipping into gourmand.

options.label: Smoky and churchy — frankincense and myrrh leading, not labdanum
options.note_to_perfumer: Frankincense and myrrh lead instead of the usual labdanum-benzoin pair — smoky and resinous, closer to a censer than a bottle.

options.label: Floral amber — rose and jasmine folded into the resin
options.note_to_perfumer: Rose and jasmine folded into the classic labdanum-benzoin base — the warmth still leads, but there's a real floral heart inside it now, not just a hint.

options.label: Spiced amber — cardamom and pepper running through the resin
options.note_to_perfumer: Cardamom and black pepper cut into the resin the way they would in a real oud-and-amber attar — spice as texture, not garnish.

options.label: Fresh amber — a citrus top over the resin, lighter and more modern
options.note_to_perfumer: A citrus top laid over the same labdanum-benzoin base, ambroxan instead of a heavier resin for the drydown — the modern, lighter reading of amber.

options.label: Fruit — something sweet cutting through the resin
Dark berries — blackcurrant, jammy over warm resin
options.note_to_perfumer: Dark berries over a warm labdanum-benzoin amber — blackcurrant and damascone's jammy top, iso E super for lift, no oud underneath at all.

options.label: Mango, ripe and creamy, melting into the amber
options.note_to_perfumer: Creamy tropical mango melted straight into the amber's own sweetness — gamma-undecalactone and fructone for the fruit, vanillin rounding it out, nothing woody enough to compete.

options.label: Peach, soft and velvety, warmed by the resin
options.note_to_perfumer: Soft, velvety peach warmed by labdanum and benzoin rather than cooled by oud — the fuzzy-skin lactone facet sitting directly in the resin.

options.label: Green apple, cutting sharp through the sweetness
options.note_to_perfumer: Fresh green apple cut sharp against the amber's warmth — cis-3-hexenyl acetate for the bitten skin, bergamot to lift it, the resin still doing most of the talking underneath.

options.label: Rose, with berries steeped underneath it
options.note_to_perfumer: Rose Wardia and blackcurrant steeped into the labdanum-benzoin base — a floral-fruity amber, no oud shadow the way the mukhallat version carries one.

options.label: Bright citrus cutting through all that resin
options.note_to_perfumer: Bright bergamot and orange cutting straight through the resin — the amber kept warm and thick underneath rather than reduced to a whisper.

I-expert-chypre-detail.text: Which chypre, exactly? The triangle bends ten different ways.

options.label: Classic — bergamot, rose, and a mossy floor, the true triangle
options.note_to_perfumer: The chypre triangle at its most textbook — bergamot's top, rose and jasmine's heart, patchouli and peatmoss standing in for oakmoss, labdanum for warmth. The reference the other nine bend away from.

options.label: Fruity — a peach-plum facet running under the moss, like the classics did it
options.note_to_perfumer: Beta-damascone and gamma-undecalactone stand in for the peach-plum facet the old aldehyde-fruity chypres built around — a jammy fruit note worked into the moss, not sprayed on top of it.

options.label: Floral — rose and jasmine take over, the moss goes quiet
options.note_to_perfumer: The floral heart pulled all the way forward — rose and jasmine at real strength, the mossy base still there but reduced to a floor, not a competing voice.

options.label: Leather — dark, animalic, closer to a cuir than a floral
options.note_to_perfumer: Civet at absolute trace and a heavier labdanum/patchouli base turn the chypre leathery and dark — the floral heart still present but demoted, this reads as cuir first.

options.label: Aldehydic — sparkling top, powdery heart, the vintage move
options.note_to_perfumer: Two aldehydes at the top open it sparkling and slightly soapy before a rose-and-methyl-ionone heart settles in over the mossy floor — the classic vintage aldehyde-chypre move.

options.label: Woody — patchouli and cedar forward, drier than the floral read
options.note_to_perfumer: Patchouli and cedar pushed past the floral heart entirely — dry and mossy, the floral reduced to a supporting hedione facet rather than a named note.

options.label: Spicy — pepper and clove worked into the moss
options.note_to_perfumer: Black pepper and clove bud cut into the mossy floor — spice as an accent inside the chypre structure, not its own layer on top.

options.label: Fresh — a lighter, more citrus-forward chypre, less moss
options.note_to_perfumer: The moss cut back hard and the citrus doubled — a chypre built to feel light and bright rather than dense and dark.

options.label: Amber — the base gone warm and resinous, closer to an ambery chypre
options.note_to_perfumer: Labdanum and benzoin pushed well past the classic ratio — the mossy floor stays, but the whole base leans warm and resinous instead of dry and green.

options.label: Clean — a modern skin-musk chypre, the moss barely a memory
options.note_to_perfumer: The classic triangle reduced to its outline — moss and patchouli barely present, clean musks doing what the base used to do. A chypre for someone who wants the shape without the weight.

I-expert-fougere-detail.text: Which fougère, exactly? The lavender-hay handshake bends ten different ways.

options.label: Classic — lavender, hay, oakmoss, nothing modern about it
options.note_to_perfumer: The fougère as it was invented — lavender and hay against oakmoss and moss-root, nothing softened for modern taste. The reference the other nine bend away from.

options.label: Fresh — citrus and lavender, barely there base
options.note_to_perfumer: Lighter-handed than the classic build — citrus pushed forward, the oakmoss floor barely there, coumarin cut back so it never turns sweet.

options.label: Woody — vetiver and cedar doing the talking, dry all the way down
options.note_to_perfumer: Vetiver and cedar take over from the lavender — dry, rooty, closer to a woody-aromatic than a soft fougère.

options.label: Spicy — pepper and geranium sharpening the lavender
options.note_to_perfumer: Pepper and geranium worked into the lavender's own spice-facet rather than layered on top of it — the fougère read through a spicier lens.

options.label: Sweet — tonka and vanilla pushed forward, the modern gourmand read
options.note_to_perfumer: The 'fougère gourmande' move — tonka's own sweetness pulled out and amplified with vanillin and benzoin until the hay note reads more dessert than herb.

options.label: Aquatic — a marine facet laid over the lavender-hay handshake
options.note_to_perfumer: The 90s aromatic-aquatic move — dihydromyrcenol and floralozone laid over the same lavender-coumarin spine, sea air instead of hay.

options.label: Leather — patchouli and a dark base under the lavender
options.note_to_perfumer: Patchouli and labdanum turn the base leathery and dark — the lavender now sits on top of something closer to a chypre's mossy floor than a clean fougère base.

options.label: Green — sharp, bitter, almost savage
options.note_to_perfumer: Clary sage and cis-3-hexenyl acetate push the green facet as sharp and bitter as this palette allows — the aromatic side of fougère, none of the softness.

options.label: Amber — the base gone warm and resinous instead of mossy
options.note_to_perfumer: Oakmoss's usual dry-moss floor swapped for labdanum and frankincense — warmer and more resinous, the fougère read through an amber lens.

options.label: Clean — modern minimalist, mostly musk and air
options.note_to_perfumer: The lavender and hay reduced to a whisper, everything else stripped back to clean skin-musk — a fougère for someone who wants the shape of one without any of its volume.

I-expert-top.text: The opening — what should arrive first, before anyone gets close?

options.label: Bright citrus
Green and cut
Aldehydic sparkle
Spice, straight away
Nothing. Let the base speak from the first minute

I-expert-heart.text: And the heart — what should still be there two hours in?

options.label: Rose or jasmine, unmistakably floral
Whole spice — cardamom, clove, saffron
Green and herbal, not floral
Warm and gourmand
Minimal — let base and top handshake directly

B2-sea.design_note: The coast splits harder than any other anchor — low tide and cut lime are barely the same memory. Getting this branch right is most of what makes the marine and citrus shelves reachable.

options.label: Low tide. Weed, iodine, something turning
The wind off it, three streets inland
Salt dried on your own arm
The boats. Rope, wet wood, diesel
The sellers at the front. Cut lime and ice
Something with a rind you'd break with a thumbnail
Figs — the leaves more than the fruit
Blossom. It hasn't set fruit yet
Windfall. Half of it on the ground, going over
Nothing. It's between seasons

B2-barber.design_note: The fougère anchor. Everyone has been in one and nobody has a rehearsed answer about it, which is the whole point of the indirect route.

options.label: The hot towel
Whatever's in the blue jar
Talc. On the neck, at the end
Leather. The chair, mostly
Cigarettes, from the men waiting

B2-treasure.text: And what kind of treasure is it?
B2-treasure.design_note: Each option here is deliberately specific enough to skip a B3 texture drill-down — six distinct accords (b2t-chest/deep/map/money/coins/gold in data/accords.json), each built from materials that actually support the described smell (see materials.json's metallic/mineral/inky/golden facets).

options.label: Buried in an old chest, wood and leather
options.note_to_perfumer: Cedarwood and Vertofix for dry, worn wood; Oud Oliffac for the leather hinges; Norlimbanol for a dry animalic-amber shadow; Safraleine at a low dose for the spice sealed in with everything else.

options.label: Just pulled up from underwater — wet, briny, barnacled
options.note_to_perfumer: Ambroxan for salty mineral amber, Geosmin at trace for wet stone, Peatmoss for damp algae, Floralozone for ozonic brine, Vetiver EO for wet root.

options.label: An old map, ink fading on the parchment
options.note_to_perfumer: Methyl Ionone Gamma is the parchment itself, Cedarwood the pencil-line dryness, Cypriol at a low dose the ink, Coumarin the hay-dust, Frankincense the cool dust in the air above it.

options.label: Stacks of old paper money
options.note_to_perfumer: Galaxolide for cotton-linen banknote paper, Aldehyde C-12 MNA for the crisp metallic edge of a freshly counted stack, Cypriol at a trace for ink, Methyl Ionone Gamma for dry powder.

options.label: A handful of coins, cold in your palm
options.note_to_perfumer: Aldehyde C-10 and C-12 MNA for the sharp cold metallic sparkle, Dihydromyrcenol for a soapy-metal edge, Ambroxan underneath so it reads as mineral skin rather than cleaning product.

options.label: Gold and jewels, catching the light
options.note_to_perfumer: Labdanum and Benzoin for warm honeyed amber, Ethylene Brassylate for genuinely golden musk, Safraleine for jeweled saffron-leather, Frankincense so it never tips into dessert.

options.label: First light. Nothing's warm yet
Noon, and there's no shade anywhere
After dark. Everything still warm from the day
Out of season. Grey, empty, cold
Cut grass, still wet
Dust. It hasn't rained in weeks
Leaves going soft. It smells sweet and slightly wrong
Stone. A wall, a step, something built

B3-barber-deep.text: And what did you walk out into?

options.label: Cold air. It caught the back of your neck
Heat, and the street
Rain, starting
Evening. You were going somewhere after

I-ref-like.text_gift: Is there something in the collection that already feels like them?

B2-nightmarket.text: And what's the smell that pulls you toward a specific stall?

options.label: Charcoal smoke off the grill
options.note_to_perfumer: The stall with the longest line is always the one with smoke pouring straight into the street.

options.label: Sugarcane being pressed fresh
options.note_to_perfumer: The machine groans, the cane splits, and something bright and grassy-sweet hits the air before the glass is even full.

options.label: Incense smoke from the stall selling it
options.note_to_perfumer: Nobody's buying, everybody's stopping — the whole aisle smells like a temple that also sells plastic toys.

options.label: Chili oil hitting a hot pan
options.note_to_perfumer: The one stall that makes everyone cough a little and go back for more anyway.

options.label: A fortune teller's candle, burning low
options.note_to_perfumer: A single candle stub, a folding table, a queue of people who all swear they don't believe in this.

options.label: Cheap perfume testers, sprayed too generously
options.note_to_perfumer: Every bottle on the table promises to be an original. None of them smell like each other, or like anything you've smelled before.

options.label: Wet pavement as the last stalls pack up
options.note_to_perfumer: Buckets of water go down over the stall's footprint, and for a second the whole night market smells like rain instead of food.

options.label: A coconut, cracked open on the spot
options.note_to_perfumer: The machete comes down twice, a straw goes in, and it's the coldest thing in the entire market.

options.label: Corn roasting over open coals
options.note_to_perfumer: A squeeze of lime, a rub of chili salt, and it's gone before you've walked to the next stall.

options.label: The last lantern's oil, burning down to nothing
options.note_to_perfumer: One stall left, one flame left, and the whole market gone quiet enough to hear it hiss.

B2-ruins.text: What's the first thing you actually noticed?

options.label: Mildew, blooming across old plaster
options.note_to_perfumer: You can smell the water damage before you see it — a slow, patient rot that's stopped trying to hide.

options.label: A rusted iron gate, seized half-open
options.note_to_perfumer: It doesn't open all the way anymore. Nobody's fixed it, and by now nobody's meant to.

options.label: Feathers and dust in the stairwell
options.note_to_perfumer: Something lives here now that isn't anyone who used to. The stairs still hold, mostly.

options.label: Sun cutting through a hole in the roof
options.note_to_perfumer: One clean beam of light, thick with floating dust, in a room that otherwise wants to stay dark.

options.label: A basement, still half-flooded
options.note_to_perfumer: Nobody's gone down there in years. The water doesn't move, and neither does the smell.

options.label: Stacks of newspaper, yellowed and stuck together
options.note_to_perfumer: Someone was saving these for something. Whatever it was, it didn't happen.

options.label: Ivy pulling a wall down, one stone at a time
options.note_to_perfumer: Give it another ten years and there won't be a wall left to hold it up.

options.label: The last look back, before you leave
options.note_to_perfumer: You always look back once. This time it's just an empty room, and somehow that's the part you remember.

options.label: A struck match, lit once and left to burn out
options.note_to_perfumer: Someone was here recently enough to want light. Not recently enough to still be here.

options.label: Old paint, faded to almost nothing on the wall
options.note_to_perfumer: Whatever it said, the wall's worn it down to a suggestion of colour instead of a message.

B2-tailor.text: What's the smell you'd take home with the suit?

options.label: Chalk marks on dark wool
options.note_to_perfumer: The tailor never measures twice. The chalk line is always exactly where the seam will go.

options.label: Steam off a freshly pressed shirt
options.note_to_perfumer: The iron hisses, the crease sets, and for a second the whole shop smells like a held breath let go.

options.label: A mouth full of pins, mid-fitting
options.note_to_perfumer: Not a word spoken until the last pin's placed. Then it all comes out at once.

options.label: A measuring tape, worn soft at the edges
options.note_to_perfumer: It's been recalibrated by hand a hundred times and trusted more than the machine that made it.

options.label: New leather, cut for the collar
options.note_to_perfumer: It'll soften with wear. Right now it's stiff enough to hold its own shape without you in it.

options.label: A finished suit, still on the hanger
options.note_to_perfumer: It hangs there for exactly one day before somebody comes to collect it.

options.label: Spools of thread, and a can of starch
options.note_to_perfumer: It smells faintly of a hospital and nothing like one — just very, very clean.

options.label: The three-way mirror, and the silence in front of it
options.note_to_perfumer: Everyone stands a little straighter in this room. It's not the suit. It's the mirrors.

options.label: A tray of brass buttons, waiting to be sewn on
options.note_to_perfumer: Each one gets picked up, turned over once, and set down in exactly the right place.

options.label: Someone else's cologne, still in the fitting room
options.note_to_perfumer: You never meet them, but for a minute the room is unmistakably somebody else's.

B2-rooftop.text: What actually made it feel worth climbing up there?

options.label: Candles, lit because there's nothing else to do
options.note_to_perfumer: Nobody planned this. Somebody just found the candles first.

options.label: A whole city, suddenly dark at once
options.note_to_perfumer: For once you can actually see the stars, and everyone on every rooftop is looking up at the same time.

options.label: Someone's radio, running on batteries, three roofs over
options.note_to_perfumer: You can't make out the words, but everyone's humming the chorus anyway.

options.label: Clothes, left on the line, drying in the heat
options.note_to_perfumer: Somebody remembers them halfway through the evening and it becomes an excuse to stay up there longer.

options.label: Kite string, coated in glue and glass dust
options.note_to_perfumer: It's for tomorrow's kite fights, but tonight it's just something to do with your hands in the dark.

options.label: Chai, made on a gas stove and carried up the stairs
options.note_to_perfumer: It comes up the stairs before anyone's asked for it. Somebody always thinks to make it.

options.label: Lightning, close enough to smell before it hits
options.note_to_perfumer: Everyone counts the seconds without meaning to. This time nobody gets past three.

options.label: Water finding a new way down, through a broken gutter
options.note_to_perfumer: It's been dripping onto the same spot for two years. Somehow it's still not annoying.

options.label: Jasmine vines on the neighbouring wall, soaked through
options.note_to_perfumer: It grows wild over the next wall and nobody's ever cut it back. Tonight you're glad of that.

options.label: The one dry hour, right before the power comes back
options.note_to_perfumer: Everyone knows it's ending soon. Nobody says so, and nobody goes back down early either.

B2-pottery.text: What's the part of the process that stays with you?

options.label: Wet clay, spinning on the wheel
options.note_to_perfumer: The wheel spins, the clay rises, and for a minute the whole room smells like the bottom of a riverbed.

options.label: An unfired pot, dry and pale, waiting for the kiln
options.note_to_perfumer: It's fragile now in a way it never will be again — one wrong knock and it's dust.

options.label: The kiln itself, radiating heat from across the room
options.note_to_perfumer: Nobody opens the door until it's ready. You just stand near it and feel the whole room get drier.

options.label: Rows of glaze, in jars along the back wall
options.note_to_perfumer: Each jar is labelled in handwriting only the potter can read anymore.

options.label: The first attempt, cracked and set aside
options.note_to_perfumer: It sits on the shelf for months. Eventually it becomes a doorstop instead of a mistake.

options.label: Wet hands, wiped on an apron that's given up being clean
options.note_to_perfumer: It's stiff enough now to stand up on its own. Nobody's ever suggested washing it.

options.label: A finished piece, still warm, glaze catching the light
options.note_to_perfumer: It's not for sale yet. For now it just gets passed around the room so everyone can hold it once.

options.label: The water bucket, gone murky grey by the end of the day
options.note_to_perfumer: It gets thrown out at closing and the whole yard smells like a riverbank for an hour.

options.label: Fine dust, settled on every shelf in the room
options.note_to_perfumer: Only the pieces actually being thrown this week are dust-free. Everything else waits its turn.

options.label: The teacher's hands, guiding yours on the wheel for the first time
options.note_to_perfumer: For about ten seconds the pot actually looks like it might turn out even. Then they let go.

B2-stadium.text: What's the smell that means the match is actually starting?

options.label: The floodlights, warming up before the match
options.note_to_perfumer: They flicker once, then hold — and every single person in the stadium looks up at the same time.

options.label: Freshly cut grass, right at the boundary rope
options.note_to_perfumer: It's the only part of the ground that still smells like a garden instead of a crowd.

options.label: Roasted peanuts, in a twist of newspaper
options.note_to_perfumer: Everyone's hands are a little oily by the fourth over. Nobody minds.

options.label: The roar of the crowd, right after a six
options.note_to_perfumer: The ball's already in the crowd somewhere. Nobody's watching the fielders chase it — everyone's still standing.

options.label: Sunscreen and sweat, hours into an afternoon match
options.note_to_perfumer: Reapplied twice, worn off anyway. By the last session nobody's bothering anymore.

options.label: A brand new ball, straight out of the box
options.note_to_perfumer: It'll be scuffed and re-shined a dozen times before the day's out. Right now it's perfect.

options.label: The announcer's voice, a little static over the tannoy
options.note_to_perfumer: Half the words get lost in the feedback. The crowd fills in the rest anyway.

options.label: Popcorn and samosas, from two different vendors at once
options.note_to_perfumer: Both vendors are somehow always sold out by the tea break, and both always claim they weren't ready for it.

options.label: Walking out, right before the final over
options.note_to_perfumer: The whole ground goes quiet for exactly as long as it takes to reach the crease.

options.label: Team colours, faded and dusty by the last day of the series
options.note_to_perfumer: Nobody's washed it since day one of the series. Superstition, mostly.

B2-atelier.text: What's actually sitting in front of you right now?

options.label: A fresh blotter strip, before anything's on it
options.note_to_perfumer: It's the only honest moment in the whole process — before the material decides what it is.

options.label: The alcohol base, before a single drop's been added
options.note_to_perfumer: It has to disappear completely once everything else is in. For now it's the loudest thing in the room.

options.label: A mistake, left in an open vial to dry out and reconsider
options.note_to_perfumer: Wrong in every obvious way. Kept on the shelf anyway, in case it's right for something else entirely.

options.label: The reference bottle from years ago, still on the shelf
options.note_to_perfumer: Half the cork's worn away from being opened and closed for comparison, year after year.

options.label: Raw materials, lined up on the bench, not yet touching
options.note_to_perfumer: Nothing here is a perfume yet. It's just a row of decisions that haven't been made.

options.label: The exact moment a blend finally clicks
options.note_to_perfumer: You don't always know why it works. You just know, immediately, that it does.

options.label: A formula, crossed out twice and rewritten in the margin
options.note_to_perfumer: The numbers in pen win, eventually. But the pencil ones underneath are still legible if you look.

options.label: The last drop, before the vial's completely empty
options.note_to_perfumer: You tip the vial and wait. Sometimes there's one more drop. Sometimes there really isn't.

options.label: The smell of concentration itself — nothing, and everything
options.note_to_perfumer: No smell describes this one honestly. It's the moment right before the smell exists.

options.label: An unlabelled sample, from nobody remembers when
options.note_to_perfumer: Nobody's brave enough to throw it out, in case it turns out to be the good one.

B2-hillstation.text: What cuts through the fog first?

options.label: Pine, and air cold enough to see your breath
options.note_to_perfumer: The path's barely visible ten feet ahead. The pine is the only thing you can be sure of.

options.label: Woodsmoke, from a fire you can't see
options.note_to_perfumer: It never gets any closer. You just follow the smell and hope.

options.label: Moss on a boulder, soaked through with mist
options.note_to_perfumer: It's been wet for so long it's stopped being able to imagine dry.

options.label: A tea stall, the one warm point on the whole road
options.note_to_perfumer: Everyone stops here, whether they meant to or not. Nobody regrets it.

options.label: Fog, condensing on a cold window
options.note_to_perfumer: You wipe a clear patch and it's fogged over again before you've finished looking.

options.label: Mule bells, somewhere below on the switchback path
options.note_to_perfumer: They come up the same path every day, whether the fog's in or not.

options.label: Rhododendron, blooming red through the grey
options.note_to_perfumer: It's the only flower stubborn enough to bloom at this altitude, this late in the year.

options.label: An old colonial guesthouse, all creaking wood and damp carpet
options.note_to_perfumer: The heater's never quite enough. Nobody who stays here minds.

options.label: Cardamom, growing wild on the terraced slopes
options.note_to_perfumer: You can smell the plantation a full switchback before you can see it.

options.label: Clouds, seen from above for once instead of below
options.note_to_perfumer: For about ten minutes, right at the top, you're above the whole grey mess instead of inside it.

B2-cinema.text: What's the smell that means the film's about to start?

options.label: Butter popcorn, from the counter outside
options.note_to_perfumer: You buy the large one every time, promising yourself you won't finish it before the trailers end.

options.label: Air conditioning, hitting velvet seats
options.note_to_perfumer: Whatever the temperature outside was, it's forgotten within thirty seconds of sitting down.

options.label: A ticket stub, fresh ink, still slightly warm from the printer
options.note_to_perfumer: It goes in a pocket and gets found again three weeks later, unexpectedly.

options.label: The curtain, pulling back just as the lights fully dim
options.note_to_perfumer: Half the room still checks their phones. The other half actually watches it happen.

options.label: Samosas, bought fast during the interval
options.note_to_perfumer: You always misjudge the queue and end up eating it standing in the dark aisle, mid-scene.

options.label: A stranger's perfume, two rows back
options.note_to_perfumer: You never see their face. For two hours, they're just a scent in the dark.

options.label: A cold soda, sweating in the cup holder
options.note_to_perfumer: It's gone before the second act. Nobody plans that, it just always happens.

options.label: The lights coming up as the credits roll
options.note_to_perfumer: Half the room's already standing before the last name finishes scrolling.

options.label: The hall, emptied out, one usher sweeping up
options.note_to_perfumer: It takes the usher twenty minutes to clear one screening's worth of mess. Nobody envies the job.

options.label: Walking out into daylight you weren't expecting anymore
options.note_to_perfumer: It always takes a second too long to remember what time of day it actually is.

B2-cargo.text: What's actually stacked in the hold with you?

options.label: Sacks of spice, stacked to the ceiling
options.note_to_perfumer: You can taste the air before you've even opened a single sack.

options.label: Tar, sealed into every seam of the hull
options.note_to_perfumer: Every plank's been sealed by hand. It's the only reason any of this is still afloat.

options.label: Rope, crusted white with dried salt
options.note_to_perfumer: It's stiff enough now to stand on its own coil, salt holding every fibre in place.

options.label: The captain's ledger, ink smudged from a wet hand
options.note_to_perfumer: A hundred crates, a hundred numbers, and not one of them can be wrong at the port.

options.label: Crates of dried fish, packed for the long voyage
options.note_to_perfumer: It's not pleasant exactly. It's just what the whole lower deck smells like, and eventually you stop noticing.

options.label: Sacks, soaked through in a monsoon crossing
options.note_to_perfumer: Half the manifest will need rewriting once they see what actually survived the crossing.

options.label: The captain's cabin, oil lamp still burning at 3am
options.note_to_perfumer: Everyone else on board is asleep by now. He never quite is.

options.label: Something brought back from a foreign port, still in its wrapping
options.note_to_perfumer: Nobody on board can identify it. That's exactly why it got bought.

options.label: Dawn at the docks, the hold finally being unloaded
options.note_to_perfumer: Every crate that comes off is one less thing this crew has to be responsible for.

options.label: The ship's cat, asleep on the warmest crate
options.note_to_perfumer: Nobody remembers whose cat it originally was. It's been three ports since anyone asked.

B2-fridayfeast.text: Which feast, and what's actually cooking?
B2-fridayfeast.design_note: Rain+cooking is the flagship leaf here — the user's exact brief was petrichor plus Friday non-veg cooking. No literal meat material exists in this palette; the savoury register is built from spice leads + guaiacol's char + a ghee-lactone + civet at genuine trace, the same honest-approximation approach the rest of this library already uses for food.

options.label: Rain on a Friday afternoon, with the cooking already going
options.note_to_perfumer: The rain lands first — real Kannauj clay attar and geosmin, not a synthetic ozone guess. Underneath it, cardamom and saffron for the pot already on the stove, guaiacol at trace for the seared edge of frying spice, a ghee-rich lactone for the fat in the pan, and civet at an almost-nothing dose for the savoury depth no gourmand accord usually bothers with. This is an impression of a very specific Friday, not a replica of a curry — food doesn't translate to fragrance one-to-one, but this is the closest this palette gets.

options.label: Mutton curry, simmering after Friday prayers
options.note_to_perfumer: Whole spice first — cardamom, clove, black pepper, the way they go into the pot before the meat does. Safraleine and civet at trace carry the savoury-leather weight real mutton has simmering for hours; guaiacol is the smoke off a pan that's been on the heat too long in the best way. No literal meat note exists in fine fragrance — this gets close by leaning on the same spice-and-warmth architecture the kitchen itself is built on.

options.label: Biryani — rice and whole spice, for the whole family
options.note_to_perfumer: Safraleine leads here rather than supports — biryani is a saffron-and-rice dish first, a meat dish second. Hedione stands in for the steam rising off the handi when the lid finally comes off; delta-decalactone is the ghee poured over the top layer. Whole spice (cardamom, clove, nutmeg) rather than ground, for the ones people pick out and leave on the side of the plate.

options.label: The mosque courtyard, emptying into the street
options.note_to_perfumer: Not food at all — the ten minutes after, when the courtyard empties and everyone's own attar and cologne mix together in the open air over the dust of the street. Safraleine and Oud Oliffac for the mukhallats half the crowd is wearing, dihydromyrcenol for the fresh outdoor air, Iso E Super underneath so it reads as a crowd of people rather than one person.

options.label: Eid morning — sevaiyan and cardamom milk
options.note_to_perfumer: Sweet rather than savoury on purpose — Eid morning starts with sevaiyan, not the feast. Two milk lactones do the work of warm, sugared milk and toasted vermicelli; cardamom keeps it from turning into a plain dessert accord; rosewater is the one spoonful sprinkled on top before it's served.

options.label: Eid feast — meat shared with the whole street
options.note_to_perfumer: Heavier and more generous than the Friday curry — labdanum adds the richness of a feast meant to be shared beyond one household, not just one meal. Same honest limitation as every food-coded accord in this library: guaiacol's char and civet's trace-animalic warmth are the closest approximation fine fragrance has for cooked meat, not a literal copy of it.

options.label: The table, set for everyone, before anyone's eaten
options.note_to_perfumer: Anticipation rather than the meal itself — everything's plated, everyone's washed their hands, and someone's still saying the du'a. Benzoin and bergamot keep it warm and bright rather than heavy; a general feast note, not tied to one specific occasion, for wherever the flow lands on a customer without them having named Friday or Eid specifically.

options.label: Iftar — dates and the first sip of water
options.note_to_perfumer: The single most restrained accord in the set on purpose — Iftar isn't the feast, it's the relief right before it. Floralozone is the first sip of water; gamma-undecalactone and delta-decalactone together are as close as this palette gets to a date's sticky sweetness without tipping into a full dessert accord.
